imageCompressor.privacyNote: Photos never leave your device — everything is processed locally. Saved files have EXIF metadata such as GPS location and camera info removed.
imageCompressor.skippedFiles: {n} file(s) were skipped (not an image or over 50MB).
imageCompressor.targetHint: Automatically finds the highest quality that fits, and reduces resolution if it still doesn't. 1KB is counted as 1,000 bytes so the file passes any site's limit.

formatHint.original: Keeps the original format. HEIC, GIF, BMP, etc. are saved as JPG.
formatHint.webp: Compare the size and quality of WebP and JPG results. Check whether the destination accepts WebP.
formatHint.avif: Smallest files, but few sites and apps support it.
formatHint.png: Lossless — quality doesn't apply and photos may get larger.

imageCompressor.pngHint: PNG is lossless, so it barely shrinks. For photos, choose JPG or WebP.
imageCompressor.maxSideHint: Scales the longer side down, keeping the aspect ratio. Small images are never enlarged.
imageCompressor.targetMissed: {n} image(s) couldn't reach the target size and were saved at the smallest possible size. Try a larger target or WebP.
imageCompressor.compareHint: Drag the slider to compare quality. Tap another photo in the list to switch.
imageCompressor.emptyHint: Add photos and they're compressed right away. Add many at once, or paste with Ctrl+V.
imageCompressor.rowMissed: Target not reached — saved at the smallest size
imageCompressor.rowLarger: Larger than the original. Lower the quality or choose JPG/WebP.

uses.title: Recommended settings
items: Government forms & document uploads: target 200–500KB, JPG
Email & forums: target 1MB, JPG
Blogs & online store pages: long edge 1920px, quality 80%
Messengers & Instagram: long edge 1080px, quality 85%
Your own website: WebP at 75–80% (lightest)

features.title: Features
items: Drag and drop for easy upload
Quality slider to balance quality and size
Convert between JPG, PNG, and WebP
Set max width/height to resize images
Batch compress multiple images at once

formats.title: Formats
items: JPG: the safe choice for photos, accepted everywhere. Transparency becomes white.
WebP: Compare the output size and quality, and check support at your upload destination.
AVIF: smallest, but limited support and some browsers can't save it.
PNG: lossless with transparency. For logos and screenshots; photos barely shrink.
HEIC (iPhone): only Safari can open it. Compressed output is saved as JPG.

tips.title: Tips
items: If there's a size limit, use 'Target file size' — it finds the quality for you.
After reducing image dimensions, check the actual file size and whether the details you need remain.
Quality 70–85% is hard to tell apart by eye. Check with the before/after slider.
Compression removes GPS location, so photos of your home don't reveal where you live.
Lossy compression can't be undone — keep your originals.

whatIs.title: What is the Image Compressor?
whatIs.description: A browser-based image optimization tool that reduces file size for JPG, PNG, and WebP images. All processing happens on your device — images are never uploaded to a server, protecting your privacy. Use it for web image optimization, reducing email attachment sizes, pre-processing SNS uploads, and batch compressing multiple images at once.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Drop images, click to select, or paste with Ctrl+V. You can add multiple images.
2. Choose a preset or select quality adjustment or target file size.
3. Changing the format or maximum size uses the new settings. A paused queue waits for Continue processing, and failed items can be retried separately.
4. Compare before and after, then download individual images or a ZIP. The ZIP contains images completed with the current settings when you clicked.

items.q: How do I get a photo under 500KB?
items.a: Choose 'Target file size' → 500KB and add your photo. It finds the highest quality that fits and lowers the resolution step by step if quality alone isn't enough. Keep the output as JPG if the site requires it.

items.q: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Everything runs inside your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.
Yes. The image is redrawn and re-encoded, so GPS location, camera model and capture time are not kept. Orientation is applied from EXIF so the photo stays upright.

items.q: My iPhone HEIC photo won't open.
items.a: Chrome, Edge and most Android browsers can't open HEIC. Open this page in Safari on your iPhone to compress HEIC straight to JPG, or set Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible.
Re-saving an already compressed photo at high quality, or saving a photo as PNG, can increase size. Lower the quality, choose JPG/WebP, or reduce the resolution.

queue.title: Compression tasks
queue.running: Compressing one image at a time
queue.pausing: Waiting for the current operation to stop
queue.pausedHint: Adding images or changing settings keeps the queue paused. Choose Continue processing to use the current settings.
queue.cancelHint: Pausing takes effect between processing stages. A browser operation that has already started may need to finish first.
queue.zipHint: The ZIP contains images completed with the current settings when you click. Later image or setting changes do not alter that ZIP. If you request another while it is being created, only the latest request downloads.
queue.zipWorking: Creating a ZIP from the results captured when you clicked.
queue.zipFailed: The ZIP could not be created or its download could not be requested. Check the completed images and try again.
queue.restartZip: Create a new ZIP from current results
